findings.note: The round-22 changes (publication-fsync-failure fault-injection fixture, mutants M/N/O, suite tally 383 to 387) were not propagated to the sibling declared outputs - the same amendment-propagation class this package rated Major on rounds 8 and 12 and pledged to close by grep-sweep. Verified against the captures the bundle carries: (1) the CHANGELOG entry states the uncovered set is one mutant, F only, out of 12 mutants with 11 killed (A..L), and 11 fixture scenario directories, while the shipped mutation-proofs.log carries FIFTEEN mutants with THIRTEEN killed and F AND O uncovered, and the Outputs table lists TWELVE fixture directories; the entry's own tally line was updated to 387/0, so it is internally inconsistent, not merely snapshot-dated, and it understates the disclosed residual test gap on a Security-Sensitive, high-risk surface. (2) The report Files Changed section says fifteen run_t007_ functions and eleven new fixture directories; the shipped driver has SIXTEEN (grep of the capture confirms; run_t007_fsync_failure_case is the sixteenth) and the report's own Outputs table lists twelve directories - the round-19 recount lectured that a count in prose is a claim with a shelf life and then went stale again the same way. (3) The GREEN capture section asserts green-shipped logs are at 383 passed, 0 failed, which is what the Test Result field and the contract both cite - all three claims are false at shipped bytes (captures, Test Result field, and contract all say 387/0). (4) The mutation-proofs intro says the current shipped suite has 383/0 and eleven of twelve mutants are killed while listing thirteen letters, and the Regression table repeats 383/0 for the block suite. The authoritative artifacts (contract, mutation log, green/red/focused captures, MANIFEST) are consistent with each other, so this is a documentation-integrity defect, not a behavioral one - but the CHANGELOG is a permanent declared governance output and currently misdescribes the shipped verification posture.

The mutant-F note still says F and M are the pair that remain and that the round-20 counting fix and unlink-side fsync are not yet exercised - future fixture work. Both claims are contradicted later in the same log: mutant M is annotated COVERED as of round 22 (384/3) and mutant N (the counting fix) dies at 385/2. The RESULT lines are authoritative and correct; the stale hand-authored annotation inside the shipped capture should be corrected in the next regeneration.

On the success path, if journal.unlink() succeeds but the subsequent rmtree of the batch directory fails (ignore_errors=True swallows it), _discard_batch returns True and the run exits 0 silently while pre-image backups remain on disk with no journal. Because the recovery scan globs only */TRANSACTION.json, journal-less litter is invisible to every later invocation forever - the identical invisible-litter mechanism the round-1 MINOR fixed on the Prepare-failure path, reachable here through a different route. Hygiene-level: no live artifact is affected and the retained bytes stay inside the feature's own staging area.
